title: Where do data come from and what do they mean?

cues.en: -: The universe is a really, really, really unfathomably complex place, and we don't even understand how complex it actually is.
cues.zh: 宇宙是非常非常、難以想像地複雜的地方，我們甚至不了解它究竟有多複雜。

cues.en: And so, to understand our complex and mysterious universe, we build measurement devices that convert some physical observable into a number
cues.zh: 所以為了理解複雜而神祕的宇宙，我們建立測量裝置，把某種可觀測的物理量，轉成數字，

cues.en: or a set of numbers.
cues.zh: 或一組數字。

cues.en: So, here's an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: Imagine you're doing a survey questionnaire that you give to customers of some company.
cues.zh: 想像你做一份問卷，發給某家公司的顧客。

cues.en: So, the idea is that you want to understand your customers, but people are really complicated and they're diverse.
cues.zh: 目的是了解顧客，但人非常複雜，也很多樣。

cues.en: And so, you devise a measurement device, which is the survey, and you convert some aspects of people's behavior and preferences
cues.zh: 於是設計一個測量工具，也就是問卷，把人們行為、偏好，

cues.en: and decision making into a set of numbers.
cues.zh: 與決策的某些面向，轉成一組數字。

cues.en: Maybe it's yes/no answers that you code as zero or one, or maybe you ask how much they would, how much money they would pay for something,
cues.zh: 可能是以 0 或 1 編碼的是非題，也可能詢問願意花多少錢買某個東西，

cues.en: or how much they would enjoy this particular service.
cues.zh: 或多喜歡某項服務。

cues.en: So, the point here is that there are real things happening out there in the universe, and those things are measured and represented as numbers,
cues.zh: 重點是，宇宙中確實發生一些事情，我們測量它們，並用數字表示，

cues.en: and those numbers are data.
cues.zh: 那些數字就是資料。

cues.en: So, this is where data come from.
cues.zh: 這就是資料的來源。

cues.en: We develop measurement techniques to translate physical and biological phenomena into numbers that can be stored on a computer.
cues.zh: 我們發展測量技術，把物理與生物現象，轉成能儲存在電腦上的數字。

cues.en: The measurement techniques might be really technologically sophisticated, like a Super Collider or an MRI machine or an electron scanning microscope.
cues.zh: 測量技術可能非常先進，例如超級對撞機、MRI 機器，或掃描式電子顯微鏡。

cues.en: Or the measurement techniques might be really simple, like a questionnaire or a medical expert's rating of disease severity in a patient.
cues.zh: 也可能很簡單，例如問卷，或醫療專家對病人疾病嚴重程度的評分。

cues.en: But conceptually, all data are the same.
cues.zh: 但概念上，所有資料都一樣。

cues.en: You measure something in the universe, that measurement produces a number or a series of numbers, and those numbers are stored on a computer, and we call those data.
cues.zh: 測量宇宙中的某個東西，產生一個數字或一連串數字，存到電腦上，我們把這些叫做資料。

cues.en: So, aren't those data perfect?
cues.zh: 那這些資料不是很完美嗎？

cues.en: Can't we just trust the numbers immediately?
cues.zh: 不能直接相信數字嗎？

cues.en: Why do we need statistics?
cues.zh: 為什麼需要統計？

cues.en: Well, there are several problems with data.
cues.zh: 因為資料有幾個問題。

cues.en: Okay, I shouldn't call these problems.
cues.zh: 好，我不該叫它們問題。

cues.en: The are features of data, but they can pose limitations, that prevent us from being able to interpret
cues.zh: 它們是資料的特性，但可能形成限制，讓我們無法，

cues.en: the data in a straightforward manner.
cues.zh: 直接解讀資料。

cues.en: Perhaps the most severe limitation, which is almost a philosophical limitation, is that we can only gather data about what we can measure.
cues.zh: 或許最嚴重，幾乎是哲學上的限制，是我們只能蒐集關於可測量事物的資料。

cues.en: So, let me give you an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: Let's say you asked people to fill out an online survey where they report their purchasing preferences from 10 years ago.
cues.zh: 假設請人們填線上問卷，回報十年前的購買偏好。

cues.en: So, what kinds of factors influenced what they bought 10 years ago?
cues.zh: 也就是十年前，哪些因素影響他們買什麼？

cues.en: Of course, you'll get data, you'll get numbers, Maybe you'll get thousands of people to fill in your survey, lots and lots of numbers, but what do those data actually mean?
cues.zh: 當然會得到資料、數字，也許有幾千人填問卷，得到大量數字，但這些資料真正代表什麼？

cues.en: Do they really reflect people's past economic decision making, or are you actually just measuring their memory?
cues.zh: 真的反映過去的經濟決策，還是其實只在測量記憶？

cues.en: Here's another example.
cues.zh: 另一個例子。

cues.en: It gets really hot inside engines, right?
cues.zh: 引擎裡很熱，對吧？

cues.en: But it's important to measure the temperature inside an engine.
cues.zh: 但測量引擎內部溫度很重要。

cues.en: Well, here's a problem.
cues.zh: 這裡有個問題。

cues.en: Most thermometers melt if they're placed inside an engine.
cues.zh: 大多數溫度計放進引擎就會融化。

cues.en: So, you know, you might think of putting a thermometer just outside the engine, but then what is that temperature data actually telling you?
cues.zh: 可能會想把溫度計放在引擎外面一點，但這些溫度資料究竟告訴你什麼？

cues.en: In fact, it's a combination of the engine temperature, the outside temperature, and the heat transmission through the material that the engine is made out of.
cues.zh: 其實，它混合了引擎溫度、外界溫度，以及熱量穿過引擎材質的傳遞效果。

cues.en: So, the point is that you always need to think carefully about the data, where they come from, and what they actually measure, and whether they really measure the thing
cues.zh: 所以重點是，始終要仔細思考資料來自哪裡、真正測量什麼，以及是否真的測量到，

cues.en: that you are interested in studying.
cues.zh: 你想研究的東西。

cues.en: One final example, because of the time that I'm recording this lecture.
cues.zh: 再舉最後一個例子，與錄製這堂講座的時間有關。

cues.en: So, in early 2020, the novel Coronavirus was spreading around the world.
cues.zh: 2020 年初，新型冠狀病毒正在全球傳播。

cues.en: Countries were trying to get accurate counts of the number of people who were infected, but the problem was that many healthy people actually didn't realize that they were infected
cues.zh: 各國試圖準確計算感染人數，但問題是，許多健康的人其實不知道自己感染了，

cues.en: because they had no symptoms or minor symptoms that just felt like a normal cold or a flu.
cues.zh: 因為沒有症狀，或只有像一般感冒、流感的輕微症狀。

cues.en: So, in fact, what the data were actually showing is the number of reported cases, which is not the same thing as the number of infected people.
cues.zh: 所以資料真正顯示的，其實是通報病例數，不等於感染人數。

cues.en: And the problem with that is that the former number, so the number of positive confirmed cases is actually not that important.
cues.zh: 問題在於，前者，也就是確認陽性病例數，其實不是那麼重要。

cues.en: That's not a relevant number.
cues.zh: 那不是相關的數字。

cues.en: The really important number that we needed is the number of infected people, and that is really, really difficult to measure.
cues.zh: 真正需要的重要數字，是感染人數，而這非常非常難測量。

cues.en: Okay, now, there are other limitations of data that I will discuss elsewhere in this course.
cues.zh: 課程其他地方，還會討論資料的其他限制。

cues.en: For example, measurements can be noisy.
cues.zh: 例如，測量可能含有雜訊。

cues.en: Many systems, particularly people are very complicated.
cues.zh: 許多系統，尤其是人，非常複雜。

cues.en: So there can be many factors that influence the measurements.
cues.zh: 因此可能有很多因素影響測量。

cues.en: And so, the data can be misleading if you don't take those factors into consideration.
cues.zh: 若不把這些因素納入考慮，資料可能誤導你。

cues.en: So, for example, if you only measure how much ice cream people eat, but you only take your measurements in winter, then you're not going to get a very accurate picture
cues.zh: 例如，只測量人們吃多少冰淇淋，卻只在冬天測量，就不會準確了解，

cues.en: of how much ice cream is actually consumed.
cues.zh: 實際吃了多少冰淇淋。

cues.en: Okay, the most important conclusion here is that although we like to think that data come from things in the universe that we want to study,
cues.zh: 最重要的結論是，雖然我們喜歡認為，資料來自宇宙中想研究，

cues.en: things that we want to understand, that is totally not the case.
cues.zh: 想了解的事物，但事實完全不是這樣。

cues.en: Data do not come from the things in the universe that we want to understand.
cues.zh: 資料並不是來自宇宙中，我們想了解的事物。

cues.en: Data actually come from our measurement devices, and if our measurement devices are not accurate, if they're noisy, if they're imprecise or if they're biased
cues.zh: 資料其實來自測量裝置。如果測量裝置不準確、有雜訊、不精確、有偏差，

cues.en: or flawed, then the data will be very problematic as well.
cues.zh: 或有缺陷，資料也會有很大問題。
